messages:
Anna: heads up — did a cross-device kernel sweep this morning. L4/T4/A10 behave fine at seqlen<=512 but we see a sharp perf cliff for seqlen>=1024. A100/H100 keep scaling. Posting quick numbers and flame output. @Samir @Miguel :eyes:

Samir: can you paste the exact table and the command you ran? curious if KV cache usage changed across runs or if batching heuristics differed.

Anna: command: `./bench_runner --model redwood-3b --devices l4,t4,a10,a100,h100 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seqlens 128,512,1024,2048 --kv-cache`

perf-bot: perf/regression detected: PR#4321 decreased tokens/sec on device l4 by 11.8% (baseline: 7240 tok/s @seqlen512 -> 6390 tok/s @seqlen512), larger drop at seqlen2048. CI link: https://ci.redwood/perf/4321

Anna: table (tokens/sec)
```
device  seqlen128 seqlen512 seqlen1024 seqlen2048
A100    9100     8500     7800      7200
H100    9300     8800     8200      7600
A10     6800     6400     4100      3600
L4      7300     7200     4200      3100
T4      5600     5400     3300      2600
```

Anna: flame dump shows a hot kernel path: `opt_attn_v2` dominates on L4/T4 for seqlen>=1024, and we see memory allocator churn + repeated kernel re-compiles in the trace.

Miguel: sounds like the autotuner mistakenly prefers the attention-optimized kernel on low-memory Ampere/Turing parts where it thrashes the KV cache. For H100/A100 the kernel's reblocking helps, for L4/T4 it causes tiling mismatch -> extra swaps.

Samir: agreed. two actionable axes: (1) make kernel registry aware of architecture+memory-class so candidates are filtered (arch_tag: h100,a100 vs l4/t4/a10), (2) add seqlen-aware path selection: prefer fallback GEMM-based attention for seqlen>=1024 on low-memory gpus unless latency SLO requires otherwise.

Priya: also check batching heuristics — we saw different batch-size scaling on A10 vs L4. Maybe the autotuner's cost model assumes nvlink bandwidth that isn't present on T4.

Anna: quick perf diffs from microbench (seqlen1024, batch1):
```
master (autotune): L4 4200 tok/s, T4 3300 tok/s
patch (filter arch tag): L4 6100 tok/s, T4 4800 tok/s
```

Miguel: nice — filtering candidate kernels by arch tag is low-touch and seems high-impact. We should also teach the tuner to prefer kernels with linear KV memory when device_vram < 24GB.

Priya: propose a new preset and rollout plan: `preset: low_memory_inference` targeting L4/T4/A10 with overrides: max_batch=4, kv_cache_mode=streaming, kernel_preference=[gemm_attention,opt_small_mem], seq_threshold=768. This lives in runtime/presets/autotune.yaml and is opt-in for now.

Anna: example preset snippet:
```
# runtime/presets/autotune.yaml
low_memory_inference:
  devices: [l4, t4, a10]
  max_batch: 4
  kv_cache_mode: streaming
  kernel_preference: [gemm_attention, opt_small_mem]
  seq_threshold: 768
  fallback_policy: prefer_generic_if_mem_thrash
```

Jae: I'll open PR to add arch tags to kernel registry + add a quick unit test that runs the microbench for seqlen1024 on a mock-L4 profile. Will also add perf CI gate for the preset.

Samir: one more subtlety — we need to track warm vs cold KV cache. The perf cliff looks worse on cold starts because the optimized kernel is re-initializing big temp buffers. Add a KV warmup probe in autotuner so cost estimates separate cold/warm.

Anna: good point. I'll append a tiny KV probe (200 tokens) before the microbench and surface warm/cold numbers in the autotune report.

perf-bot: note recorded: perf/issue/1799123456 created -> autotune-arch-filter. Assigned: Jae. CI job added: microbench-lowmem-1799123456.

Priya: timeline idea: patch + tests by EOD, internal rollout to staging for low_memory_inference preset by mid-week, enable opt-in for a couple customers for real runs, then full default if stable.

Miguel: also add diagnostic flags to runtime to dump kernel selection trace for a request: `RUNTIME_TRACE=kernel_picks` — will help triage future regressions quickly.

Anna: perfect. thanks all. taking notes and will follow up in PR. :sparkles:
